notes: §1985:XIV.2.2.4 GR26: data-name-1 "has the format 'YYMMDD'" and holds the date the MCS recognized the message complete; it "is updated only by the MCS as part of the execution of a RECEIVE statement". The 85 arm is the communication facility itself (COBOL0902 refuses the CD at 2014+): StoredMessage#Complete stamps a message yyMMdd when its EMI/EGI completes it (or at seeding), MessageControlSession#Transfer writes it through CommunicationArea#SetReceived at positions 1-6 of the I-O area on a RECEIVE that transfers data, and every other statement (#Statement) changes only the status key. Probes at --std 85: a seeded message is dated today in YYMMDD, an explicit-date message gives its date, a message an output CD SENDs to the terminal is dated today, NO DATA and a refused (21) RECEIVE leave the moved date, a redefining group record reads the area, MESSAGE DATE written twice is COBOL6169, the 2023 RECEIVE FROM..GIVING is COBOL0900; the witness shows SEND/PURGE/DISABLE/ENABLE leave it.

next.reason: 1985: "Data-name-1 has the format 'YYMMDD' ... the date on which the MCS recognizes that the message is complete."; 2023: "No communication description entry in 2023; no candidate defines a CD message-date field.". The 2023 standard has no communication description entry. Its RECEIVE rule and the date candidates (ACCEPT, functions) do not state the CD message-date field that the MCS updates.
